## Details

<a id="ia.json-ld"></a>

### 2.1 JSON-LD present

- Stable ID: `ia.json-ld`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-08 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Add a JSON-LD block with the schema.org context to each page.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.json-ld)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-08](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.json-ld`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.json-ld

Why: JSON-LD is the preferred format for structured data in Google and AI search engines. It tells AI systems exactly what the page is about in a standard vocabulary.

References:

- [Schema.org Person](https://schema.org/Person) (spec)
- [Schema.org author property](https://schema.org/author) (spec)
- [Google E-E-A-T guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add a script element with type application/ld+json to the head of the page.

   ```html
   <script type="application/ld+json">
   {
     "@context": "https://schema.org",
     "@type": "WebPage",
     "name": "Pricing"
   }
   </script>
   ```
2. Repeat the key facts of the JSON-LD as visible text on the page.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.organization-schema"></a>

### 2.2 Organization / WebSite schema

- Stable ID: `ia.organization-schema`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-08 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Add Organization and WebSite JSON-LD with name and url to the home page.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.organization-schema)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-08](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.organization-schema`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.organization-schema

Why: Organization and WebSite schemas establish the brand identity in the knowledge graph. AI systems use them to attribute content and to build entity relations.

References:

- [Schema.org Person](https://schema.org/Person) (spec)
- [Schema.org author property](https://schema.org/author) (spec)
- [Google E-E-A-T guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add an Organization entity with name, url, logo and sameAs.

   ```json
   {
     "@context": "https://schema.org",
     "@type": "Organization",
     "@id": "https://example.com/#organization",
     "name": "Example",
     "url": "https://example.com",
     "logo": "https://example.com/logo.png"
   }
   ```
2. Add a WebSite entity with name and url that refers to the Organization as publisher.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.high-value-schema"></a>

### 2.3 High-value schema types

- Stable ID: `ia.high-value-schema`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-08 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Describe the primary content of each page with the matching schema.org type.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.high-value-schema)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-08](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.high-value-schema`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.high-value-schema

Why: Schema types such as Article, Product and FAQPage give agents typed entities to extract instead of free text. They also make the page eligible for rich results.

References:

- [Schema.org Person](https://schema.org/Person) (spec)
- [Schema.org author property](https://schema.org/author) (spec)
- [Google E-E-A-T guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (guide)

Steps:

1. Identify the primary content type of the page, for example Product, Article or Event.
2. Add JSON-LD of that type with the required properties.

   ```json
   {
     "@context": "https://schema.org",
     "@type": "Product",
     "name": "Team plan",
     "offers": {"@type": "Offer", "price": "29", "priceCurrency": "EUR"}
   }
   ```

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.entity-linking"></a>

### 2.4 Entity linking via @id

- Stable ID: `ia.entity-linking`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-08 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Give each JSON-LD entity a stable @id and refer to it from other entities.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.entity-linking)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-08](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.entity-linking`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.entity-linking

Why: Entity links through @id make a connected graph of your content. AI systems follow the references to understand the relations between entities.

References:

- [Schema.org Person](https://schema.org/Person) (spec)
- [Schema.org author property](https://schema.org/author) (spec)
- [Google E-E-A-T guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add an @id with a fragment URL to each main entity.

   ```json
   "@id": "https://example.com/#organization"
   ```
2. Refer to the entity by @id from other entities, for example as publisher.

   ```json
   "publisher": {"@id": "https://example.com/#organization"}
   ```

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

### 2.6 Schema validation

- Stable ID: `ia.schema-validation`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-08 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Fix JSON syntax errors and missing required properties in each JSON-LD block.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.schema-validation)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-08](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.schema-validation`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.schema-validation

Why: Search engines and AI systems ignore structured data that is not valid. Errors in the markup remove all of its value.

References:

- [Schema.org Person](https://schema.org/Person) (spec)
- [Schema.org author property](https://schema.org/author) (spec)
- [Google E-E-A-T guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (guide)

Steps:

1. Run each JSON-LD block through a JSON parser and fix the syntax errors.
2. Add @context and @type to each top-level entity.
3. Test the page with the IsAgentReady structured data validator.

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.faq-schema"></a>

### 2.7 FAQPage schema

- Stable ID: `ia.faq-schema`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-08 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Add FAQPage JSON-LD for the questions and answers that are visible on the page.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.faq-schema)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-08](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.faq-schema`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.faq-schema

Why: FAQPage schema exposes questions and answers as separate machine-readable pairs. An agent can then use a direct answer without parsing prose.

References:

- [Schema.org Person](https://schema.org/Person) (spec)
- [Schema.org author property](https://schema.org/author) (spec)
- [Google E-E-A-T guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (guide)

Steps:

1. Find the questions and answers that are visible on the page.
2. Add a FAQPage entity with one Question and acceptedAnswer per pair.

   ```json
   {
     "@context": "https://schema.org",
     "@type": "FAQPage",
     "mainEntity": [{
       "@type": "Question",
       "name": "Is there a free plan?",
       "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Yes. The free plan has 100 calls per day."}
     }]
   }
   ```

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.author-attribution"></a>

### 2.8 Author attribution

- Stable ID: `ia.author-attribution`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-08 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Add a Person author with name and url to the JSON-LD of each editorial page.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.author-attribution)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-08](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.author-attribution`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.author-attribution

Why: Author attribution gives agents and search engines a clear, machine-readable signal of who stands behind the content and links it to a known entity. This supports trust and provenance (E-E-A-T) and lets systems attribute the content to its author.

References:

- [Schema.org Person](https://schema.org/Person) (spec)
- [Schema.org author property](https://schema.org/author) (spec)
- [Google E-E-A-T guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add an author property of type Person to the Article JSON-LD.

   ```json
   "author": {"@type": "Person", "name": "Jane Doe", "url": "https://example.com/team/jane"}
   ```
2. Show the author name as visible text on the page.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.trust-pages"></a>

### 2.9 Trust anchor pages

- Stable ID: `ia.trust-pages`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Publish about, contact and privacy pages with real content and link them from each page.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.trust-pages)
- Evidence source: [Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines: E-E-A-T and trust](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content)
- Expected result: 200 (run the same command for /about and /privacy)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.trust-pages`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.trust-pages

Why: Agents check about, contact and privacy pages to verify a business is legitimate and to answer contact questions before recommending it. Thin or missing trust pages read as an anonymous site.

References:

- [Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines: E-E-A-T and trust](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (guide)
- [Schema.org ContactPage](https://schema.org/ContactPage) (spec)

Steps:

1. Publish /about, /contact and /privacy with real text, an address and contact details.
2. Link the three pages from the footer of each page.
3. Add ContactPage and AboutPage JSON-LD to the pages.

Verify:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://{domain}/contact
```
